title: Deployment ebb-and-flow: weekly ops journal — release & hotfix cadence
summary: Notes from the weekly ops journal focused on the last release train window (2026-03), observed post-deploy jitter, hotfix candidate triage, and a small change-log consolidation experiment. Informal log intended for rotation handoff and follow-ups.
content:
Context:
- This week we executed the March release window (canary -> ramp -> full). Traffic profile: heavy morning burst 09:00–11:00 PT, three internal load tests at 10:15.
- We saw transient tail-latency spikes on two models after canary during 10:05–10:22, correlated with KV cache evictions on a subset of nodes.

Observed incidents and triage:
1) 10:05–10:22 PT: ~3x p95 on token-gen for model-rw-13b-quant.
   - Symptom: spike in p95 token latency, small increase in error rate (0.3% -> 0.9%).
   - Root-cause hypothesis: concurrent cache reset + aggressive batching parameter change in canary config (max_batch_delay lowered from 8ms to 5ms) caused CPU contention during KV shuffles.
   - Rapid mitigations taken: rolled canary back to previous batch config at 10:24, disabled one new autoscaling rule, evicted noisy JVM process on node pool a1.
   - Outcome: p95 returned to baseline by 10:31. Postmortem ticket created: JIRA RDW-1620.

2) 14:40 PT: customer-facing error on dedicated-reserved for customer-acme (hotfix candidate).
   - Symptom: requests queued >30s for a single tenant GPU pool during a config sync.
   - Investigation: found a cron job (db-maintenance) launched on an operator node pinned to the same host as the tenant pool due to quota mislabeling.
   - Short-term fix: moved cron to maintenance nodes, increased node isolation for dedicated pools.
   - Follow-up: add node-label enforcement to preflight (see action items).

Change-log consolidation experiment:
- Goal: reduce the noise in release notes by aggregating low-risk config-only PRs into a weekly "config rollup" instead of per-release blurb.
- Ran experiment on 2026-03 config PRs: 12 small PRs aggregated into 1 rollup entry in the release notes draft.
- Feedback from product: positive (less friction for non-technical reviewers), but security team requested explicit callouts for KMS/HSM key changes.

Metrics snapshot (post-ramp):
- p50/p95/p99 token-gen: baseline 18ms / 72ms / 220ms -> post-change 20ms / 70ms / 210ms (after rollback).
- Error rate: baseline 0.28% -> peak 0.92% -> stabilized at 0.31%.
- Autoscaler churn: 4 ephemeral scale events during canary, one of which correlated with the latency spike.

Decisions made during the meeting:
- Keep the batching config at previous (conservative) defaults for full ramp for next 2 release windows. (owner: Marcus Chen)
- Add a canary checklist item: run KV-cache eviction simulation in staging before any batch config changes. (owner: Priya Nair)
- Adopt weekly config rollup for low-risk PRs, but include an "ops appendix" with explicit security-sensitive config changes. (owner: Aisha Patel + Security reviewer)

Action items (concrete):
- RDW-A1: Add node-label enforcement to release preflight and run in next dry-run (owner: Luis Alvarez, due 2026-03-18).
- RDW-A2: Implement KV-cache eviction simulation harness in staging and add to canary checklist (owner: Marcus Chen, due 2026-03-20).
- RDW-A3: Update release notes template to include ops appendix for keys, KMS/HSM, and encryption toggles (owner: Jemma O'Connor, due 2026-03-17).
- RDW-A4: Investigate autoscaler noise: correlate metrics with scale events and introduce hysteresis for ephemeral bursts (owner: Samir Rao, due 2026-03-22).
- RDW-A5: Postmortem draft for the 10:05 latency spike (link JIRA RDW-1620) and cross-link to runtime PRs. (owner: Aisha Patel, due 2026-03-15).

Open questions / risks still under investigation:
- Is there a systemic pattern when canary load tests align with customer traffic bursts? Need to compare canary start times with major customer usage windows. (data: product telemetry team)
- Does the config rollup approach hide subtle regressions for platform integrators who watch individual PRs? Consider periodic deep-dives every 6 weeks.

Notes to handoff (for next rotation):
- If you see a sudden p95 increase during canary, check active batch config commits in the last 30 minutes first.
- For dedicated tenant slowdowns, check node label overlap and cron schedules on hosts; we've seen one case of mislabeling cause direct resource contention.

References and quick links:
- RDW-1620 (latency spike) — JIRA
- RDW-1543 (dedicated pool isolation follow-up) — JIRA
- PR #478 in runtime: temporary batching tweak (reverted) — GitHub
- Slack thread: #release-ops "canary jitter 2026-03-11"

Informal / backlog scribbles (notes to self):
- Try simulated golden path with load-profiles at 2x for morning burst; see if autoscaler hysteresis triggers.
- Revisit eviction policy: maybe increase grace time by 50ms for critical model pools.
- Consider canary-phase split: small percentage of nodes with new config + separate traffic slice for external customers vs internal tests.

Meeting end: 15:05 PT. Next check-in: 2026-03-18 weekly ops journal.

Add KV-cache eviction simulation to canary checklist (owner: Priya Nair)
Adopt weekly config rollup with ops appendix for security-sensitive changes (owner: Aisha Patel + security)
